question: What are the two hourly volume thresholds in All-Way Stop Control Warrant D, and how can they be adjusted when the major-street 85th-percentile speed exceeds 40 mph?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The provided evidence does not contain the actual hourly volume thresholds of All-Way Stop Control Warrant D — those values appear in Items A and B of Paragraph 1 of Section 2B.16, which is not included in the evidence supplied. What the evidence does show is the speed-based adjustment: when the 85th-percentile approach speed on the major street exceeds 40 mph, the minimum vehicular volume warrants may be reduced to 70 percent of the Item A and Item B values. (The other provisions supplied — Sections 4C.02, 4C.03, 4C.05, and 4C.08 — concern traffic signal warrants, not All-Way Stop Control Warrant D.) Options (permitted): - "If the 85th-percentile approach speed of the major-street traffic exceeds 40 mph, the minimum vehicular volume warrants may be reduced to 70 percent of the values given in Items A and B in Paragraph 1 of this Section." Citations: - Section 2B.16 Option §2 (p.79) Note on insufficiency: The specific numeric thresholds (Items A and B of Paragraph 1 of Section 2B.16) are not present in the evidence, so I cannot state them without inventing content. If you can supply Paragraph 1 of Section 2B.16, I can complete the answer.
gold_answer: For the same 8 hours of a typical day, the combined entering volume must be at least 300 units per hour on the major-street approaches and at least 200 units per hour on the minor-street approaches. If the major-street 85th-percentile speed exceeds 40 mph, the minimums may be reduced to 70 percent of those values.
